findings.evidence: TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/Basic.lean:88-95 lists the five fields; LocalizationTopology.lean:49-51 says the construction "also asks that `J` be finitely generated and that the subspace topology on `D` be `J`-adic".
findings.fix: Reword to match lines 49-51: `D` is open and bounded, but `(D, J)` is not yet a `PairOfDefinition` — both `J.FG` and `IsAdic J` are still unproved.
findings.issue: `isOpen_locSubring`'s docstring says openness and boundedness are "two of the conditions a ring of definition must satisfy; the remaining one, that the subspace topology on `D` is the `J`-adic topology". `PairOfDefinition` has fields `isOpen_ringOfDefinition`, `fg_idealOfDefinition`, `isAdic_idealOfDefinition` — boundedness is not a field (it is the theorem `isBounded_ringOfDefinition`), and two requirements remain, not one, as the module docstring itself states at lines 49-51.

findings.evidence: Line 431 `private theorem locBasis`; line 443 `noncomputable def locTopology`; lines 20-24 list only `locSubring`, `HasDenominatorPower`, `locIdeal`, `locNhd`.
findings.fix: List `locTopology` (and `algebraMapD`) under Main definitions; drop `locBasis` from Main results or fold it into the `hasBasis_nhds_zero_locTopology` bullet without naming the private declaration.
findings.issue: `## Main definitions` omits `locTopology` — the topology the PR exists to build — and the public `algebraMapD`, while `## Main results` (line 42) advertises `locBasis`, which is `private` and unreachable by any consumer.

findings.evidence: grep for `locSubring_mono` across `TauCeti/` returns only its declaration (line 159) and this docstring line; `locSubring_empty` is used at line 585.
findings.fix: Drop the "this file needs" claim (or the `locSubring_mono` mention) and describe it as a monotonicity lemma offered for downstream use.
findings.issue: "`locSubring_le_iff`, with `locSubring_empty` and `locSubring_mono`: … the two consequences of it this file needs" is false for `locSubring_mono`, which has no use anywhere in the repository.

findings.evidence: The hypothesis appears only as an input at lines 395-399 and 431-439; nothing in the file derives it from the basis property.
findings.fix: State it as the hypothesis the construction uses ("what `locNhd_leftMul` needs, hence what every `locTopology` declaration carries"), not as a characterisation.
findings.issue: `HasDenominatorPower`'s docstring claims it "is exactly what makes the `locNhd` into a basis of neighbourhoods of zero for a ring topology" — an equivalence. Only sufficiency is proved (`locNhd_leftMul`/`locBasis`); no necessity result exists here or elsewhere in the repo.

findings.evidence: Main results at lines 51-77 and Provenance at lines 35-44 enumerate declarations; neither mentions the lemma added at line 113.
findings.fix: Add a bullet for `TauCeti.Huber.IsBounded.isPowerBounded_of_mem` to Main results and include it in the "New here" list.
findings.issue: The new public `IsBounded.isPowerBounded_of_mem` is absent from this file's `## Main results` list and from its `## Provenance` "New here are …" enumeration, both of which are otherwise exhaustive (they list even `isPowerBounded_iff`).

findings.evidence: TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/Basic.lean:91 `idealOfDefinition : Ideal ringOfDefinition`; no `ideal` field exists.
findings.issue: The Provenance section says the field rename was ``I`→`ideal``; the field is `idealOfDefinition`. Naming a field that does not exist misdirects anyone reading the port notes.

findings.evidence: Lines 27-36 list ten results; `divByS_def` and `algebraMap_mul_invSelf` are public and unlisted.
findings.fix: Add both to the Main results list.
findings.issue: `## Main results` omits two public declarations: `divByS_def` (line 67), which the file's own docstrings call the only route to the `mk'` API since the body is not exported, and `algebraMap_mul_invSelf` (line 116).

summary: Docstrings are dense and mostly accurate, but the module docstring of LocalizationTopology.lean advertises a private theorem while omitting the file's headline definition, one theorem docstring contradicts the module docstring about what is left to prove, and several claims (a lemma the file "needs", a renamed field, a necessity claim) are not true of the code.
